# Explanation

These pages cover why RECAP behaves as it does. Read them when a design
decision seems surprising and you want the reasoning, or before committing to
an approach that would be expensive to change.

They are not instructions. For steps, see the
[How-To Guides](../how-to/index.qmd); for exact signatures, see the
[API Reference](/reference/index.html).

## In reading order

1. **[How RECAP Organizes Data](01-data-organization.qmd)** — namespaces,
   the definition/record split, resource hierarchies, and the provenance graph.
   Start here.
2. **[Query Model and Loading](02-query-model.qmd)** — why queries are
   immutable, why relationships are unloaded by default, and how the identity
   map keeps one entity as one object.
3. **[Resource Loading](03-resource-loading.qmd)** — how resource trees are
   hydrated without issuing one query per child.
4. **[Authentication and Authorization](04-authentication-authorization.qmd)** —
   actors, scopes, namespace grants, and why visibility is applied before
   filtering.
5. **[Audit and Error Semantics](05-audit-and-errors.qmd)** — what is recorded
   about every mutation, and what is deliberately excluded.
6. **[REST Query and Command Architecture](06-rest-query-architecture.qmd)** —
   how remote clients reach the same behaviour as local ones over HTTP.

If you are new to RECAP, read
[Core Concepts](../getting-started/03-core-concepts.qmd) first. It covers the
same model in far less depth and makes these pages much easier to follow.
